E4-01.why: guess — four bare figure labels (Point A/B/D/C), no propositional content at all; options-only cannot discriminate. Note the letters are shuffled (C="Point D", D="Point C"), so even a position habit is unavailable. Pure guess at control.

E4-02.why: redundancy ladder — C ("and then, after that") and D ("subsequently ... after that") are both overtly padded, leaving A as the one concise alternate. Two concise legal options cannot coexist in an ACT set, so No Change (B) must be the flawed original and A is the repair.

E4-03.why: alternates bracket the error — the alternates vary only the punctuation before an appositive, which names the tested issue as appositive punctuation. Semicolon (A) needs an independent clause after it; "and a common resident" (C) makes a false compound. Comma appositive (D) is the residue.

E4-04.why: alternates bracket the error + redundancy — all four restate "the same question" and differ only in how the clause is attached. A repeats "the question", C uses the clumsy "that being whether". The colon (D) is the clean appositive attachment.

E4-05.why: rationale-quality tell in a Yes/No purpose item — B is the only option whose reason is specific, multi-part and internally consistent ("never mentions training, certification, or how she entered the field"). C and D cite mutually incompatible concrete facts (twenty hours vs a week), so at most one can be true; A is a flat generality. Partly a guess without the essay.

E4-06.why: tense-sequence singleton — C is the lone present tense in a past-tense set and drops out; between B and D, "had been renamed ... the land company had subdivided" stacks two past perfects, while simple past + past perfect (D) puts the subdividing correctly before the renaming. Would not survive a surprise from the surrounding passage.

E4-07.why: elimination-to-the-residue on NO CHANGE — A shifts to "had minded", B breaks whether/whether parallelism with "if", D shifts to present "mind". All three alternates are independently defective, so the untested original is the residue.

E4-08.why: redundancy ladder — B is the textbook pleonasm ("her own personal"), D deletes the meaning-bearing "her own". C is the concise option that keeps the content; since a correct No Change would make C equally correct, No Change must be the padded original.

E4-09.why: redundancy ladder — B ("gradually ... bit by bit over time") and D ("gradually ... over a period of time") are stacked redundancies, and D also goes passive. C is the single concise active option; No Change cannot also be concise or the item would have two keys.

E4-10.why: rationale-quality tell — B is the only option that concedes the details the Yes options lean on (the director, the helper in the beam) and explains why they still do not meet the stated purpose; D is a throwaway irrelevance ("never says which theater"). The concede-then-qualify option among flat assertions is the distractor-family formula this family leaks by. Still partly a guess.
